newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 25.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp plans to produce the Corolla and recreational vehicles (RV) in India as early as 1999, in cooperation with India's Kirloskar group. They hope to set up a joint venture by next summer, aiming for annual output of 100,000 units. Total investment will be 30 to 50 billion yen. India's vehicle demand is expected to double to around 1.3 million vehicles by 2000.

Bridgestone Corp is expected to boost its pre-tax profit by 19 percent to 92 billion yen in the business year to December 1996, up three billion yen from the initial projection. This is due to strong exports of tyres to North America and other Asian nations, as a result of the yen's weakness.

Amatsuji Steel Ball Mfg Co Ltd's pre-tax profit is seen falling by 10 percent to 3.3 billion yen in the year to March 1997, due to a weak demand from car makers. Tsubakimoto Precision Products Co Ltd is expected to see flat pre-tax profits at three billion yen.

Mitsubishi Chemical Corp plans to cut purchases of naphtha, the raw material for many petrochemical products, by 10 percent from next January. It will also cut output of ethylene and other products by about the same percentage because of a rapid increase in naphtha prices since the summer.
Marubeni Corp and the Burmese government agreed to set up a joint venture by next spring to produce rice for feed in Burma. They expect to produce 150,000 tonnes of rice by 2004.

The Canada Oil Sand consortium, which was set by 71 Japanese national oil and petroleum exploration companies, plans to start test extraction of crude from oil sands at a pace of 10,000 barrels a day in Canada from 2001. It hopes for commercial extraction of 100,000 barrels a day in 2008, and to import the crude from Canada.

Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd has started negotiating the rights to digital TV broadcasting in Britain with British Telecommunications Plc, BskyB Plc and others. Matsushita hopes to set up a joint venture shortly and begin broadcasting in 1997.
